RiskAverseTech/toolgate: Already adapted in jevalan as the tool.risk capability (`node ${TOOLGATE_CLI} decide`).
qkal/Canny: Completion gate backed by a local ledger.
Brainwires/jevwire: General-purpose kit with seven MCP tools and a shared library.
GhalebDweikat/winnow: Its MCP tools expose recall and statistics, not a verdict: deciding which blocks to keep returns transformed content, so it does not fit the hub's outcome model.
tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction: Returns a rewritten message array, not a verdict: the hub has nowhere to put that output.
shitianfang/wakegate: Pure library (shouldWake) with no plugin, CLI or MCP. jevalan already covers the same decision with the agent-wakeup flow, without the extra runtime.
Yaxin9Luo/spending-effort-with-jev: Claude Code mod: it registers inside the host and exposes no callable surface outside it.
ruban-24/switchboard: Launcher/proxy for claude and codex: its classifier is internal and publishes no decision surface the hub could route to.
Dicklesworthstone/skillranker: CLI with JSON output and dry-run, offline and shadow modes: the cleanest candidate for an exec specialist.
JoaquinRuiz/medula: Local server with SQLite and a demo app: it would fit as an http provider, but it carries its own write state and lab scaffolding.
typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js: Client SDK: it is transport to a backend, not a specialist the hub can ask.
typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-python: Client SDK: it is transport to a backend, not a specialist the hub can ask.
typesafe-ai/system-one-adapter-python: Backend bridge: exposes any OpenAI-compatible LLM as a System One client, so it serves behind a flow, not as a specialist.
BillionsBobby/JevRouter: `route` takes a JSON request plus candidates and returns a typed decision with Jev's probabilities intact and the `router` field kept separate. Measured by us: it decides without ever executing, leaves a receipt, filters by permission, asks for confirmation on high risk, abstains on low confidence, an option it did not offer, a 500 or a non-JSON reply, and refuses without a key (27 cases with a simulated provider, 25 pass; an unknown command and --version print the help and exit 0). Against the real model (typesafe/jev-1.13 through OpenRouter, 9 cases, about 0.0002 USD) it routes tests, search and deploy correctly, orders a three-step plan and is not won by a poisoned description, but an embedded instruction moved Jev to 0.64 for deploy_prod and only the router's confidence gate stopped it. A permission-filtered candidate is still sent to the model, a malformed risk silently becomes low, and a secret in the request text reaches the provider. Server, MCP and dashboard were not measured.
GodsBoy/jev-agent-skill-router: `jev-router route` takes a request and a catalog and returns `route`, `no_skill` or `review` with the probability of each call; it never loads or runs a skill.
TheoOliveira/pi-jev: Almost entirely a Pi extension, which cannot be called from outside.
gargpratyush/jev-router: A Claude Code and Codex launcher and proxy: it picks the model tier on every turn inside its own process.
rhighs/jev-code: An SDK for building decisions and an interactive coding agent, not a decision to serve.
mizchi/jev-lint: Natural-language linter: an ast-grep matcher picks the code and a model is asked one sentence per match. Measured by us without a key and always with --dry-run: it plans and prices a run without sending anything, the matcher selects what its rules document, suppressions work, and a 52-fragment frontier shows the matcher reaches 41 of 44 constructs it should judge (it misses generator functions, bash <(curl ...) and a doc comment on an arrow function). A path that does not exist exits 0 and there is no --version. No model verdict was measured.
supercorp-ai/supercov: `quality` scores each file with yes/no questions and `quality patch` reviews only a change; `security` asks twelve checks per file.
lakeday-org/perch: Scans a whole repository and outputs a findings table with severity and confidence; `perch check <id>` re-asks about a single one, which would be a yes/no.
NiazMorshed2007/jev-review: A single MCP tool, `jev_review`, returning a 1-to-10 score with confidence per quality dimension.
keeltrace/hermes-nerve: A supervisor plugin living inside Hermes, which keeps the authority to stop or continue.
rbalch/typesafeai-review: `ts-review`: a code reviewer where code is in charge. It runs deterministic checks, splits the diff, asks Jev typed questions per chunk and composes the `APPROVE` / `CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `NEEDS_HUMAN` verdict in code.
DanRWilloughby/snifftest: Prose linter with fifteen rules: five countable ones (dashes, colons, sentence rhythm, filler vocabulary and your own banned-word list) that are local regular expressions, and ten judgment rules that need a model. Measured by us without a key: the five countable rules do what the documentation promises, including its exemptions, and a 67-text frontier catches 41 of 42 defects with one false alarm (a literal use of a listed word). The judgment rules were not measured.
iamtoomas/JevLint: Natural-language convention rules; returns the probability that each file breaks them against a threshold (`--threshold`). Measured by us without a key and always with --dry-run (npm @jevlint/cli 0.1.4): it prints the requests without sending anything, the file selection skips node_modules, dist, secrets/credentials and non-JS/TS files, configuration and --ignore work, and without a key it refuses (exit 2). Findings: no --version, and without a config the default scan includes tests and .d.ts files. No model verdict was measured.
Tech-Byte-Frontier/jevgate: Review gate that parses the repository, builds evidence units (function, file schema, copy pair, test) and asks Jev typed questions about each one.
scale-venture-partners/riff: Prose linter with ruff-style rule codes: 69 rules, 61 semantic ones that call a model and 8 static ones in plain Python, plus your own phrase and regex rules that run offline. Measured by us without a key and always with --no-jev: all 28 cases pass, the static rules flag what the documentation says and respect their exceptions, and without --no-jev and without a key it refuses (exit 2) and offers --no-jev instead of silently skipping the semantic rules. The 61 semantic rules were not measured.
suraj-phanindra/wellposed: Linter for Jev requests: 45 deterministic structural checks that need no key, plus optional semantic checks with `--semantic` that do need a typesafe key. Tested by us: 18 cases passed.
NomenAK/jev-tools: Six tools for pi, omp and any MCP client: navigate unfamiliar code, ask typed questions about repository evidence, review changes and pick tests.
kindintelligence/jev-rust-review: Claude Code plugin for reviewing Rust: an MCP server runs rustc, Clippy and cargo-semver-checks filtered to the change, and Jev triages and verifies the findings.
ariel-frischer/jevkit: Generic Jev command-line client: the caller supplies the questions (`noul`, `choice`, `score`) and the text, so there is no domain decision to serve.
jsk4581/jev-blindspot: Prompt reviewer that runs next to Claude Code and Codex CLI, decides on each submission whether a review is needed and shows the result in a local web UI.
ReadycodeAI/readycode-reader: MCP server to question PDFs, Word documents and spreadsheets: finds passages, checks them with Jev and returns exact citations and calculations.
PenDraga/paperless-jev: Docker container with a web UI that classifies new documents in a Paperless-ngx inbox (type, correspondent, path, date and tags).
jon-devlapaz/tink-route: Picks a specialist skill from a Tink library, verifies `tink mount` and hands it over.
lazniak/jevskill: Agent skill whose `jev_query.py` script asks a typed question (noul, choice or score) about a state and returns the answer with `--json`.
iamvatsalpatel/tiershift: `tiershift route "<request>"` decides without calling any answering model: prints the tier (fast, medium, high), the signals that raise it and the reason; `--json` gives the full object.
redreamality/jev-skill-selection: Keep/drop gate before the first message: loads a closed skill catalog and `select --json` returns `kept`, `dropped` and the characters saved.
E-FL/typesafe-as-a-judge: Dual plugin for Codex and Claude Code with a bounded-judgment MCP server.
typakon4/jev-layer: Layer that lets an agent choose from a bounded set without handing over control: `jev_route` picks among the capabilities the host provides and `jev_record_execution` attaches the outcome; cases replay offline. Measured by us: the layer filters by permission before talking to the model, never executes, redacts secret-named context keys and fails open to a fallback on a 500, a malformed response, a missing key or an option that was not offered (17 cases with a simulated provider). Against the real model (typesafe/jev-1.14 through OpenRouter, 10 cases, about 0.0004 USD) it routes tests, search, email and deploy correctly with confidence 1, repeats the same choice five times, is not moved by an embedded instruction (0.15) or a poisoned description (0.11), and falls back on a nonsense intent (0.27). A secret written in free text, rather than under a secret-named key, does reach the provider. MCP, adapters, vision and supervision were not measured.
Mandrilsquad1441/jev-model-router: Plugin and MCP server that, given a task, returns the best model and reasoning effort plus three alternatives (smartest, fastest, cheapest that works) and the exact command to switch.
JussCubs/jev-conductor-router: Uses Jev to decide whether a task needs a Conductor cloud workspace, how hard it is and which harness and model should run it.
maker-KK/todo-jev: Classifies a request and recommends a path (local rule, decision or skill, or large model) using 20 skill profiles.
lomeshdutta/skill-router: Claude Code CLI that, at session start, ranks installed skills against the user's goal and answers: load one, none, or search skills.sh.
Bodila51/Jev-chooses-a-LLM: Cursor plugin whose MCP tool `jev_route` decides the tier (cheap, balanced, smart) and can delegate to subagents; the SDK `--run` mode also creates an agent with the resolved model and needs `CURSOR_API_KEY`.
xinyao27/jevonian: Local OpenAI-compatible proxy (127.0.0.1:8787/v1) between the agent and its providers: picks a model each turn, respects quotas and logs the decision in a cost ledger.
dirien/jev-router: Pass-through proxy for Claude Code and Codex CLI that asks Jev for the tier (fast, balanced, advanced) on every new human message and forwards the session.
iefnaf/pi-jev: Pi extension suite (selective context compaction and per-turn model routing) enabled with `pi config` and living in Pi's hooks.
miniLV/Jev-Auto-Router: `jev-codex` starts the real Codex and adds `Jev Auto Router` to the model picker: it asks Jev once per user turn and pins the model for the whole tool loop.
ansidium/jev-codex-bridge: Bridge that selects model and reasoning effort for an optional Codex session using the existing login; the proxy only runs while `jev-codex` is open.
tonyzdev/pijev: Terminal coding agent built on Pi, with Jev choosing skills, ranking code excerpts and diagnosing tool failures.
Charlyhno-eng/jev-codex-pilot: Full local software-request workflow: tickets on a Kanban board, a 1-to-5 complexity score and execution with Codex at the right model and effort, with human review and Git delivery.
wellkilo/codex-jev-preflight: Codex hook that, before each task, injects routing metadata (task type, complexity, risk and execution mode) as advisory context.
guanghuang/coding-router-jev: `codex-jev` and `claude-jev` launchers that wrap each agent's real CLI and route its turns through JEV, plus a Pi extension.
nexibeo/jev-organize: Reads every file in a folder and classifies it with Jev by department, document type, sensitivity, date and counterparty; writes a catalog, `INDEX.md`, an HTML report and, on request, an organized copy without moving the originals.
Koushik890/jev-firewall: PreToolUse hook for Claude Code and Codex: deterministic rules plus Jev, answering `allow`, `ask` or `block`.
harshwasan/jev-sentinel: Guard for coding agents with one set of checks across three hosts (a Pi extension and Claude Code and Codex hooks). Measured by us without a real key: with no key every tool call asks and none is allowed; with a placeholder key and Jev unreachable it denies changes to the host's or its own settings by deterministic rule, but an unreadable or empty event exits silently (equivalent to allowing) and the protected-path rule is bypassed by building the path with a variable. Model-dependent checks were not measured.
godspede/construct-auto-classifier: Effect-based safety gate for coding agents' shell commands (Antigravity, OpenCode and external harnesses): decides what the command does, its reversibility and blast radius, not keywords.
ursuciprian/reflex: Pre-execution gate for shell commands in Claude Code, Codex, opencode and pi, environment-aware and with team policy.
moezubair/check-risk: Turns a Git change into a risk level and score, reasons, required checks and reviewer groups; usable as a CLI with `--format json`, a GitHub Action or a TypeScript API.
caiovicentino/jev-shield: Semantic MCP firewall: a stdio proxy between any MCP client and server that inspects calls, results and tool descriptions, with deterministic structural checks and calibrated Jev probabilities.
h0j5bz0adh0-stack/jev-pilot: Python library with `decide` (picks among candidates, returns winner, confidence and probabilities), `guard` (judges a proposed command or mutation, returns `allowed` and `danger_score` against a threshold) and `check_stuck`.
dr-dimitru/claude-jev-plugin: Claude Code plugin with hooks that judge Bash, Write and Edit calls before running and Bash output afterwards; it states it is not a sandbox and that Claude Code permission rules remain the hard control.
qinpei-dev/permit-mcp: Execution-control layer for MCP agents: an `ActionProposal` goes to a deterministic policy, an optional decision provider, a one-time permit and an executor, with `allow`, `review` or `deny` outcomes.
DevMortimer/pi-warden: Guardrails for Pi that correct the agent instead of interrupting it: detects a claimed "done" without tests having run and feeds the warning back to the agent.
bojansandhaus/jev-decisions-hermes: Hermes plugin adding tools to review a plan, check the sources of an answer and judge whether a task is really finished.
numerous-com/dgp: Experimental protocol for decision-based AI, with a Jev adapter and a runnable example; independent of who evaluates (deterministic resolvers, other models and people use the same contracts).
agencyenterprise/jev-recipes: 80+ TypeScript recipes (route, rerank, gate, grade, compare, label…), each a function that takes the data, calls Jev and returns a typed result with `status: "ready"`, or the review output when the choice is uncertain.
eran-broder/jev-skills: Claude Code and Codex plugin that removes every skill from the context window and lets Jev decide each turn which ones the model sees (fixed cost of 0 tokens).
libingzheren/Jev-Mem: Code for the "Jev-Mem" paper: a System One controller organizes memory and guides retrieval (semantic, temporal, causal and entity relations) and a language model synthesizes the answer.
Avinash-jetwani/jevmem: Saves decisions, rules, bugs, tasks and failed approaches from your Claude Code chats into `JEVMEM.md` and retrieves the relevant ones next session.
ibrahemid/jevprune: Filters long command output for agents according to the task description, keeping the lines with their original text and order.
CheshiAI/Cheshi: Preview desktop app for macOS (Apple Silicon, Tahoe 26 or later) with conversation memory and CodeGraph, a local indexing and graph-query engine.
thruwire/foreman: Asynchronous Python runtime with two concurrent loops: coding agents work (Codex, OpenCode, Hermes or dcode) while a semantic supervisor watches and judges them with named probabilities.
zjunlp/JevLoop: Runnable agent-loop harness that sends every fork (act, which tool, is it safe, is it done) to a decision model (Jev or Laya) and leaves only the writing to the LLM; ships a web UI and needs no key or dependencies.
jvsteiner/jevex: Minimal agent-loop experiment where Jev drives control flow and a LangChain chat model writes the argument values and final answer, over three local MCP servers with 12 tools.
mizchi/jev-test-filter: Reads a `git diff`, asks Jev how much that change could alter each test's result (one shared state, one question per test, a single round trip) and prints filter arguments the test runner already understands.
PyModel/jev-judge-mcp: Stdio MCP server with fifteen typed-judgment tools over Jev (verify, check, filter, classify, rerank, decide, compare, extract, review, score…): the agent supplies evidence and an enumerable question and a policy decides.
emreozyoruk/hush: Issue and pull-request triage that abstains when unsure: label, spam, missing information and duplicate, each with a configurable threshold; if it is not reached it does nothing and explains why.
sharziki/semdecide: `grep` by meaning and `jq` for judgment: `is` (predicate), `choose` (route between options with each probability and confidence), `score` (ranked rubric), `filter` (JSONL) and `guard` (action-safety recipe: allow, escalate…). Measured by us with a made-up key against a simulated local provider (not Jev), so what was measured is the wrapper: exit codes 0/1/3/4/2 follow its README, a 500 is retried (three requests) and a 401 is not, malformed or out-of-range responses are provider failures, errors are versioned and redacted, filter keeps order, guard fails closed, and invalid input or a missing key sends nothing. What Jev actually answers was not measured. Also measured against the real model (typesafe/jev-1.13 through OpenRouter, 14 clear-cut cases, 14 pass, about 0.0004 USD): account takeover 0.89 vs 0.03 for a newsletter, routing and scoring are right with confidence 1, filter keeps the two churn-risk tickets and guard blocks an unrequested production wipe. An instruction embedded in the text raises the probability to 0.35 without changing the verdict. Ambiguous cases, run-to-run stability and latency were not measured.
sufianetaouil/every: Asks a yes/no question of every function in a codebase and returns each one's probability, sorted, with a threshold (`--above`) and `--json`. Measured by us without a real key (PyPI every-cli 0.1.0): everything that asks the model needs a key, so we measured what happens before the first request, i.e. which code leaves the machine. It splits nine languages into functions, chunks the rest, and skips dependencies, build output and generated files. Findings: files named secrets or credentials are judged and would be sent, and its tree-sitter dependency downloads native grammars on first use and, if it cannot, silently finds zero functions. No model answer was measured.
jyatesdotdev/jev-logtriage: Collapses a batch of logs, asks Jev six questions in a single call and code applies the thresholds to assign `suppress`, `watch`, `review`, `notify` or `page`.
hemanth/pkg-gate: Pre-install gate for npm packages: judges the lifecycle scripts of a manifest (or a loose command) and answers allow, block or warn with a structured JSON report. Measured by us without a key: it blocks curl-to-shell and credential theft and warns on system recon, but its offline engine is a list of regular expressions rather than Jev, anything it does not recognise is allowed (rm -rf $HOME in a postinstall passes), and --version prints a hard-coded number. The model-backed engine was not measured.
1jehuang/jev-pr-labeler: Semantically labels a GitHub pull request with OpenRouter's Decisions API: type (one), area (several), platform, attention (`breaking-change`, `security`) and size by conceptual scope, not by lines.
Bentlybro/siftr: Four read-only tools for coding agents: `search` (which file does this issue touch), `read` (which parts of a file matter), `pick` (which test file covers it) and `filter` (relevant parts of a log).
egma-ai/jev-code-reviewer: End-to-end PR review app: a local server, a Chrome extension that replaces code with its logic on the "Files changed" page and a CLI (`analyze`) that ranks each change by priority with Jev.
browser-use/jev-ultrafast: Browser agent with an indexed action space: given a goal, Jev picks operation and element in one request (`CLICK`, `TYPE_TEXT`, `SELECT`, `SCROLL_*`, `WAIT`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`) and a small LLM only writes the text.
krw82/jev-playwright-mcp: MCP proxy over the official Playwright server with a judgment layer inside: classifies page state (access wall, captcha, error, limit, paywall…), masks instruction injections and prunes snapshots by objective.
ismaelsoilet/jev-harness: "System 1.5" decision layer for a coding agent's quality loop, deterministic first: test-failure triage, death-loop breaking, completion veto. Tested by us (offline engine only): 18 of 21 cases passed.
ItisShikhar/gg-friggin-ez: Profanity and toxicity filter for Node.js over Jev, built for real-time game chat and moderation (50 to 500 ms): detects leetspeak, spaced or stretched characters, mixed scripts and romanized languages (Hindi, Tamil…).
caiovicentino/jev-risk-check-provider: x402check: pre-payment risk-check provider for agents and wallets (x402 PR #2422 format).
caiovicentino/jev-align: Calibrated alignment checker for model answers and agent plans: one Jev call (about 800 ms) scores signals such as sycophancy, deception ("says it ran all 47 tests and did not") or scope creep, and returns `pass` or `flag`.
ShuhanSun/jev-oas-sentinel: Compares two OpenAPI documents in two layers: deterministic structural rules and bounded semantic Jev questions about descriptions, examples, defaults, retries, ordering, pagination, authorization and error semantics.
Kushwho/jev-codes: Audits a `git diff` against editable standards packs, hunk by hunk, with one parallel Jev call per hunk; Jev writes no code, it answers typed questions with probability.
Kungie/gut: Judgments as a line of Python (`gut.likely`, classify, score) that return yes, no or `gut.UNSURE`, with `ask_human` to hand doubtful cases to a person; thresholds come from words (`lean`, `stakes`), not numbers.
openlayer-ai/jevals: Evaluations and guardrails for agents using decision models instead of an LLM judge: every evaluation of a trace comes out in a single request.
kyu1204/jgrep: `grep` for what code does rather than what it is called (published on npm as `jevgrep`): no index, no embeddings, one Jev call per chunk.
uehaj/sys1grep: `grep` by meaning: for each line Jev answers with a probability to "does it match sense X?" and a threshold applies; senses combine with AND, OR and NOT, and it works across languages.
reachjalil/jevlogs: Scores each log entry before spending on analysis: diagnostic value from 0 to 100, priority and probability of being actionable; confidently low-value ones can skip an LLM analysis branch.
qualixar/jev-decision-layer: Decision layer for assistants: given a bounded choice (task, tool, skill or review), Jev returns a typed answer with confidence, the local layer checks it and leaves a receipt, and the host keeps authority.
Ravinder82/jev-flash-router: MCP decision-routing server with zero output tokens: evaluates context, diffs, logs or plan options and returns a choice (about 150 ms, `output_tokens: 0`) through OpenRouter's Decisions API.
doronp/jevc: Compiler that turns a prose rule ("NEVER commit unless the user asks") into a Jev program: a few typed questions and a reducer that computes the verdict in ordinary code, so the rule becomes an invariant. Measured by us offline (npm jev-compiler 0.1.0): scan classifies the rules of an AGENTS.md, compile turns a JSON Schema into a typed module and says what it cannot lower, compile --lift prints the request without calling a model, emit-policy writes toolgate and bouncer YAML, and check replays all 58 recorded fixtures. --help exits 1. The offline check compares a recording with itself, so it cannot fail; live re-measurement was not run.
keltokhy/jlink: Record linkage with the matching rule written in English: `jlink.link(a, b, entity=..., on=..., definition=...)` uses Jev's pairwise judgments (Noul), with local candidate blocking and match resolution.
kinde-starter-kits/jev-agent-authorizati: Starter kit (Jev Gatehouse) that checks each agent tool call before running it: Kinde verifies the user's token and permissions and denies if one is missing, and the remaining calls go to Jev.
simota/tenbin: Repository for using the System One API from a coding agent at design time: documentation and an MCP server (question checking, evaluation, batch evaluation to calibrate thresholds, reranking, taxonomy exploration…).
killerz3/jevalyzer: Reads the chat logs coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, opencode, Gemini CLI, Antigravity) leave on disk, scores each exchange with Jev through Vercel AI Gateway and looks for where the agent went wrong.
parth-kp/jev-mail-classifier: Classifies the inbox with Jev and, according to a configuration, labels, moves, flags and notifies.
carlosedm10/agi-jev-containment: Local observation-and-response stack for agents in an isolated environment (FastAPI, React/Vite and Neo4j, with Docker): receives tool events, hides secrets, writes a JSONL tape and scores intent with Jev and Sentinel.
vnmoorthy/siege: SIEGE: a customer-support agent with real tools (refunds, address changes, discounts) facing a room of 200 people trying to make it fail; each call passes through a pre-filter written by the defender.
apixly-ai/jev-filter: Semantic filtering of agent tool results: turns large outputs (search results, full code symbols, correlated logs) into compact typed decisions before they enter the context.
DataZooDE/anofox-decide: DuckDB extension that brings natural-language decisions into SQL: `decide_probability(text, 'A refund is requested.')`, `decide_choice(text, 'Which team owns this?', [...])` and an ordered scale.
YehuiTang0316/jev-nlgrep: Searches code, documents, logs and text by meaning with natural-language conditions (supports Chinese queries) and combines text, format and structure conditions.
Hexdigest123/typesafe-comment: Code-comment linter: scores each comment on five heuristics (usefulness, readability, accuracy, redundancy and coverage) and those under the thresholds raise warnings and make the process exit non-zero.
AntonioCoppe/jev-harness: TypeScript library that turns Jev's answers into production-ready actions: a policy (answers to `notify`, `suppress`, `place`, `skip`…) and a confidence gate (if low, review, escalate or suppress).
ddfeyes/jev-mode: Takes repeated semantic judgments out of the agent's context (which team owns a ticket, whether a file is stale, whether a message reports a failure, which category a row has): you send an item and a map of typed questions.
EugeneBoondock/jevsql: Adds Jev judgments to SQLite: compare records by meaning, pick the exact evidence in a text, rerank retrieved passages, route the uncertain to a review queue and detect that a changed source invalidates a claim.
shivam2003-dev/typesafe-triage-guard: Three composable judgment pipelines over Jev: support-ticket triage (routes and prioritizes with a safety guard), observability-alert triage and a deployment-risk gate.
ntedvs/commentcop: CLI that judges JS and TS code comments with Jev: reads each comment with the surrounding code, scores accuracy and usefulness out of 100 and shows the weakest first.
rlaope/jeval: Measures how much a classifier's confidence is worth and turns the cost of an error into the threshold where the machine should stop deciding and a person start; outputs an offline-openable HTML and a YAML the app reads.
abhixhek/jevcal: Measures a typed-decision model on the user's data, picks the threshold that meets their accuracy target, computes what share of traffic still needs an LLM and fails CI when a model update breaks it.
Kadihx/jev-x-kit: Universal framework for autonomous decision-making, deep research, planning and self-improvement, packaged as a Claude Code plugin, an MCP server and a CLI.
Merth1470/jev-research-mcp: Self-hosted MCP server with one main tool, `research`, that uses Jev as the evidence-selection layer in an agent's web research: filters twice (search results before downloading and content blocks after).
tumf/jev-cli: Unofficial CLI and stdio MCP server for the Jev API: send text or a JSON state, ask typed questions (`noul`, `choice`, `score`) and receive machine-readable answers; several questions per request.
Sheltercosmo/jev4pg: PostgreSQL 14 to 17 extension with 41 Jev operators (filter, extract, rank, match, verify), explainable embeddings, an evidence cache, controlled retries and a workspace with its own HTTP API and app.
